title: FinFET Inspection - Stacking Faults Detection on Puma 9xxx
subtitle: Pre-Diffusion Quality Validation for 14nm Node Manufacturing
author: Lisa Johansson

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Puma 9xxx system to detect and classify Stacking Faults defects during pre-diffusion inspection at the 14nm technology node. The test is conducted at Milpitas Fab A to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 300mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Stacking Faults defects that are critical to yield at the 14nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Puma 9xxx platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Puma 9xxx
- Inspection Type: FinFET Inspection
- Target Defect: Stacking Faults
- Process Step: Pre-Diffusion
- Wafer Size: 300mm
- Technology Node: 14nm
- Fab Location: Milpitas Fab A

This test case applies to all Puma 9xxx systems deployed at Milpitas Fab A for pre-diffusion monitoring in the 14nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Puma 9xxx
Software Version: v13.2.881
Recipe: FINFET_INSPECTION_14nm_PRE_DIFFUSION
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Medium (148 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.1μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: Full wafer sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Puma 9xxx system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'FinFET Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Stacking Faults defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 14nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 96 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 98% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±1.3% for FinFET Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.98 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-02-05
Wafers Tested: 23
Total Defects Found: 4564
Defect Density: 645.67 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 3.9%
Capture Rate: 88.7%
Test Duration: 382 minutes
System Uptime: 97.9%

Result Classification: FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Puma 9xxx demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Stacking Faults at the 14nm node.

b) The capture rate requires optimization of the detection algorithm.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Cross-correlation with the reference SEM confirmed classification accuracy.

e) Recipe portability between systems at this fab was confirmed.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Re-tune detection algorithm thresholds for Stacking Faults at 14nm node.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Escalate to R&D for algorithm enhancement if re-tuning does not resolve sensitivity gap.
